findings.message: the verdicts are text-to-cad general rules (version 2026-11-10): general practice drawn from published design guides, and text-to-cad's own floors where no guide states a limit (each labelled by its source), no shop's limits
findings.hint: for a named shop, compare the measurements with its own published limits, or use its skill

summary: OK 1d3676a8-b091-5dfb-bfa0-fefce3663592: printing fdm: 757201 mm3, 1 body(ies); overhangs under 45 deg 0 mm2; walls min 1.1314, p05 5, median 5 mm; support ~1786.39 mm3

scale.note: it reads 319.4 mm across: a plausible size

overhangs.method: each down-facing face's angle from horizontal off the plate; a slope, ceiling or cantilever under area_floor_mm2 below the limit, or a cantilever reaching under reach_floor_mm (the nozzle given, else one bead), is listed with counted false and judged by no rule: text-to-cad's own floors, no guide states them

wall_thickness.method: exact rays into the material from samples on every face, each to the first face it crosses that looks back along it (within 45 deg); none within a knife edge's thin depth that starts or lands on its flanks. Sampled (each item sampled: true): a face's thinnest sample; the listed items under 5 mm refined to the exact least distance to the face across (refined: true) where it runs within 45 deg of both faces' normals and nothing lies between; the field's figures are the samples'

gaps.method: exact rays out of the material from samples on every face, to another face of the same part (not a neighbour, not the same hole), each face's narrowest refined to the exact least distance to the face across (refined: true) where it runs within 45 deg of both faces' normals and nothing lies between

details.method: steps between parallel planes up to step_ceiling_mm high, by sides of any surface; a step is a detail while it is narrower than across_below_mm (text-to-cad's own figure: no guide states one) and its steps bound the raised top or the sunk floor all round (an island or a pocket: text, a logo, a mark); wider, or a step running on across a face, is the part's geometry, which the walls and gaps judge

clearances.method: each pair of parts' triangulations (thinned to points_per_side) find their nearest faces; BRepExtrema measures those face pairs exactly where the triangulations come within 1.5 mm (plus their margin); farther pairs keep the triangulations' distance

trapped_volumes.method: sealed voids exactly, from their own shells; from a voxel field, air wider than its way out (a ball fits in it that cannot leave), whatever its shape; each opening's throat measured on the surface (exact: true), or read off the voxels to two voxels; escape holes the exact holes from a cavity to outside, every other opening's throat measured on the triangulation

knife_edges.method: convex edges whose material angle, read along the edge, falls under knife_below_deg: angle_deg the least, length_mm the stretch under it; the material at d from such an edge is 2 d tan(angle / 2) thick: thin_depth_mm is where it reaches min_wall_mm

support_volume.method: column fill under every down-facing surface under the angle limit, down to the part or the plate, from a raster of the triangulation along Z

sections.method: the largest ball each part's material holds, from its voxel field (to a voxel); thicker than measured_up_to_mm reads at_least

rules.title: text-to-cad general rules
rules.note: general practice: per technology the first published design guide's figure (Hubs, then Protolabs, then Xometry); the build volume the printer's given, else a typical machine (Hubs's: a desktop FDM or SLA printer), assumed; no printer's or shop's own limits
